text: Images, VM, and monitoring have each been validated on their own. This lesson tests them together, the way a real customer and a real on-call engineer would actually experience the system.

Each isolated check passing doesn't guarantee the whole system works together. A page could load fine but reference a broken image URL. An alert rule could exist but be silently misconfigured. End-to-end testing means walking through the system as a user and as an on-call engineer, not just checking each piece alone.

A real checklist: load the catalog homepage and confirm it renders. Browse at least three different product categories, not just one. Confirm every image loads from its Blob Storage URL, with nothing still pointing at the old on-prem path. And check the Activity Log for a clean resource history across the whole project.

Then trigger the alert for real -- a short CPU-stress command on the VM, left running past the five-minute window, should actually produce an email to the Action Group. A command finishing without an error only proves the rule was created, not that it works.
Just as important: confirm the alert resolves once CPU drops back down. An alert that fires but never clears is its own configuration problem, as real as one that never fires at all.

Once this checklist passes -- rendering, images, clean history, alert fires and clears -- the migration is actually ready for cutover, not just assumed to be. Next lesson writes all of this up for the team.
